messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: service:frontend /generate returning elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts in us-east-1 (p95 latency spike). Alert rule: frontend.5xx_rate > 1.5% for 3m :rotating_light:
ana: I'm getting paged — looking now. seeing a surge of 502/504s in the dashboard, mostly from prefix-cache reads. :thinking_face:
sasha: I'm oncall for runtime, joining. any correlate with deploys?
mike: No deploys in last 30m. infra shows a KV-prefetch backlog increasing. possible eviction cascade.
ana: adding logs from edge gateway:

```
2026-03-15T14:08:23Z ERROR http: upstream 504 gateway timeout route=/generate id=abcd status=504 backend=prefix-kv node=kv-7
2026-03-15T14:08:24Z WARN  prefetch: queue_size=842 inflight=56 ttl_evictions=120 host=kv-3
```
jordan: Customer-impact ping — CS reports 3 large customers saw errors in last 10m in APAC. flagging high priority.
sasha: looking at KV metrics: eviction rate spiked 10x; heartbeat misses on a subset of prefix shards -> they start returning transient 5xx. suspect corruption vs resource exhaustion.
mike: I'm SSHing into kv-3 and kv-7 now. lucy, can you open a live trace for a failing request id=abcd?
lucy: trace collected. attaching snippet: `kv_prefetch: miss -> remote_read -> timeout 2.5s -> upstream 504`
ana: mitigation ideas: 1) throttle/disable prefetch on hot prefixes 2) scale up prefetch workers 3) fail-open to read-through from backing-store 4) temporarily route traffic to fallback model pool that uses direct reads (higher cost).
sasha: quick check: config 'prefetch.enabled=true' global. we can flip to false for the hot shard set via service flags. I'll prepare a rollout.
mike: while sasha prepares the flag change, I'll reduce prefetch concurrency on kv-3/kv-7 to reduce eviction churn:

```
# on kv nodes
sudo systemctl set-environment PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=8
sudo systemctl restart prefetch-worker
```
ana: applying the flag in 2m. rolling to 3 pods in us-east-1 first. will watch errors.
(3 minutes pass)
ana: flag rollout started -> prefetch disabled for shard-range 128-255 in us-east-1 :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: NOTE: Alert suppressed due to mitigation action (rule: frontend.5xx_rate).
sasha: preliminary: 5xx rate dropped from 2.3% -> 0.9% within 90s. p95 latency still elevated but trending down.
jordan: CS update: customers report degraded but improved. one had retries and eventual success. marking as partial impact.
mike: I still see heartbeat flakiness on shard kv-7. running diagnostics:

```
$ kubectl logs kv-7 -c kv-sync | tail -n 50
ERROR shard-sync: missed-heartbeat delta=12s peer=kv-3
WARN compaction: paused due to high mem-pressure
```
sasha: mem-pressure looks high on kv-7. increasing node's heap limit might help short-term, but long-term this looks like a prefetch-induced working set blowup.
lucy: suggestion: enable read-through fallback when prefetch returns timeout so frontend can try backing-store instead of returning 504 immediately. small code change but we can flip a runtime flag.
ana: do it. flip read-through on for the hot prefix range. we'll accept higher latency for success.
mike: read-through flag enabled for us-east-1 hot-range. observing immediate drop in 504s but p99 latency hits for those keys (~3.2s). overall 5xx now 0.4%.
jordan: notifying affected customers with a short message: "we're seeing elevated errors in us-east-1 driven by cache prefetch/backpressure; mitigations in place; you may see higher latencies for certain requests."
sasha: plan for next hour: 1) schedule rolling restart of kv-7 (mem pressure) 2) audit prefetch heuristics for hot prefixes 3) permanent limit on global prefetch concurrency and circuit-breaker. I'll create tickets after handoff.
nana: prepping pager handoff. oncall until 15:30 UTC — I'll remain on-call and watching. handing to eng-sre for overnight monitoring.
mike: started rolling restart on kv-7 -> `kubectl rollout restart ds/kv-node -l shard=kv-7` . monitoring metrics.
(5 minutes)
mike: kv-7 restarted, mem pressure cleared, heartbeat stable. no new 5xx spikes.
nana: summary for postmortem: root cause: prefetch worker backlog + aggressive prefetch heuristics led to working set blowup on subset of KV shards; that caused mem pressure, heartbeat misses, eviction storms and downstream 504/502s. mitigation: disabled prefetch for hot-shard-range, enabled read-through fallback, reduced prefetch concurrency, restarted impacted nodes, scaled up pool temporarily. customer impact: partial — ~3% of traffic in us-east-1 experienced 5xx/timeouts during 14:06-14:25 UTC, affecting a small set of customers in APAC. next steps: tuning heuristics, circuit-breakers, improve observability on prefetch queue, run chaos test for cache eviction scenarios.
lucy: creating handoff note in incidents channel and opening postmortem ticket: PM-4728. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre.
nana: thanks all — I'll update the incident timeline in the ticket and do a brief runbook add for emergency prefetch-disable. :thumbsup:
